title: duplicate method not duplicate child node state
body: ### Tested versions Godot Engine v4.5.1.stable.official.f62fdbde1 - https://godotengine.org Vulkan 1.4.312 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti ### System information Godot Engine v4.5.1.stable.official.f62fdbde1 - https://godotengine.org Vulkan 1.4.312 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: NVIDIA - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1660 Ti ### Issue description I implemented a Ghost2D node to copy the target Node2D node every 0.1 seconds to create motion blur/trail effect. It works well when I only copy a single Sprite2D node. I only copy the Body node. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8310af59-b1bc-49bb-89fb-e42bd2a78297 It can be seen that the copied Sprite2D retains the Frame property state of the original node and maintains the action at that time. However, when I modify the parent node of the uncopied Model node, which is the Body node, a problem arises. https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8830f83b-5d9a-4648-abbd-d83a60ce71fb ### Steps to reproduce My Ghost2D node code is very simple ```gdscript @icon("uid://bv5syxofsw2ok") class_name Ghost2D extends Node2D @export var node2d:Node2D @export var active:bool = false @export var auto_start:bool = false @export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE,"suffix:s") var interval:float = 0.1 @export_custom(PROPERTY_HINT_NONE,"suffix:s") var ghost_lifetime:float = 0.1 @export var color:Color = Color.BLUE var timer:float = 0 func _ready() -> void: if auto_start: active = true func _process(delta: float) -> void: if node2d == null: return if not active: return timer += delta if timer >= interval: timer = 0 var clone = node2d.duplicate() as Node2D clone.global_transform = node2d.global_transform clone.process_mode =Node.PROCESS_MODE_DISABLED clone.z_index = z_index-1 clone.modulate = color get_tree().current_scene.add_child(clone) var tw = create_tween() tw.tween_property(clone,"modulate:a",0,ghost_lifetime).set_ease(Tween.EASE_OUT) tw.finished.connect(clone.queue_free) tw.play() ``` I checked the copied nodes using remote myself and found that the state of the child nodes under the Model node is initial. That is to say, the `duplicate` method copies nodes and retains attributes only for the root node; it seems that the child nodes do not retain their attributes. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) later
